name: Support labour and birth
summary: A pregnant patient who is in labour, or booked for a caesarean, is admitted from obstetrical triage to a labour, delivery and recovery room, where a labour and delivery nurse stays with her one to one through active labour while an obstetrician, family physician or midwife leads the care. About three in ten births end in a caesarean section in the unit's obstetrical operating room, and some babies need a paediatrician or a NICU bed. The work runs at the pace of unscheduled labour around the clock: delays come from waiting for a free room, the on-call anesthesiologist or obstetrician, the obstetrical OR, and a postpartum bed for the hand-over, and long inductions hold rooms for a day or more.

baseline.org_archetype: A three-site Ontario community hospital corporation with about 4,300 to 4,700 births a year in birthing units with 16 labour, delivery and recovery rooms and two obstetrical operating rooms.
baseline.notes: Unit of work is one birth episode in the birthing unit, from admission out of triage to hand-over to the mother-baby unit. Obstetrical triage, NICU care and postpartum care are separate processes.

unit_of_work: one birth (one labouring or scheduled-caesarean patient and her baby)
trigger: Obstetrical triage confirms active labour, induction or a labour complication and sends the patient to the birthing unit, or a patient arrives for a booked caesarean section.
end_state: Mother and baby are handed over to the mother-baby unit, or the baby is admitted to the NICU and the mother is handed over alone; the birth is recorded in the chart and the BORN Information System.

volume.seasonality: Births run slightly higher from July to October and lower in winter months; daily arrivals are random, so several patients can need active labour care at once.

evidence.note: 4,690 babies born in 2021/22 (391 a month) and 4,277 in 2020/21 (356 a month); the low of 333 is the organisation file's 2018/19 figure. Babies born slightly exceed births to patients because of twins.

One-to-one care in active labour (kelly2022) plus a second nurse at each birth and two in the OR; 16 rooms staffed around the clock gives about 8 to 10 nurses a shift, about 50 FTE; the rest of the 110 headcount covers triage and part-time positions.
About 60% of births are led or attended by obstetricians, plus every caesarean and consultations for family physician and midwife patients; most of their time is office and OR gynaecology.
Family physicians with obstetrical privileges attend about a fifth of births in Ontario community hospitals; author's estimate.
Midwives attend roughly one in six to one in five hospital births in Ontario; most midwifery time is prenatal and home postnatal care.
Epidurals for over half of labouring patients and anaesthesia for every caesarean, from an in-house or on-call obstetrical anesthesiologist.
Called to about one birth in ten (caesareans, meconium, preterm, abnormal tracing).
Unit clerks create the newborn encounter and keep the unit board; extended-hours coverage.

roles.title: Patient care manager, maternity or paediatrics

evidence.note: One patient care manager for the birthing units handles staffing gaps, incidents and bed flow.
Program director time on birthing unit performance, incidents and medical staff issues.

systems.name: Hospital information system (electronic patient record with ADT, order entry, results, eMAR and clinical documentation)
Operating room scheduling and perioperative documentation module
Electronic bed board and patient flow dashboard
Transfusion medicine module and blood fridge tracking
Email, telephone, pagers and wireless phones
Safety incident and complaints reporting system
Fax (referrals, requisitions and reports to community physicians)

resources.name: Obstetrical operating rooms in the birthing unit

steps.name: Admit patient to a labour room
steps.description: The labour and delivery nurse takes report from the triage nurse, settles the patient in a free labour, delivery and recovery room, checks the prenatal record (faxed from the office or viewed in the BORN system), starts an IV and draws admission bloods, and records the admission assessment in the hospital information system. When all rooms are full the patient waits in triage until one is cleaned and free.

error.defect_description: Prenatal record missing (GBS status, blood group) or allergy not recorded.

next.condition: obstetrician is the most responsible provider
family physician is the most responsible provider
midwife is the most responsible provider

evidence.note: Admission tasks and room waits from the author's knowledge of Ontario birthing units; provider shares follow typical Ontario community hospital mixes.

steps.name: Assess patient and write labour plan (obstetrician)
steps.description: The obstetrician examines the patient, reviews the fetal heart tracing, cervical examination and prenatal risks, and writes admission orders: monitoring method, group B strep antibiotics, pain relief options and whether to induce or augment labour. Overnight the order is often given by phone and the bedside assessment follows.

control.basis: Public Hospitals Act: only a physician or midwife with privileges may order treatment for an inpatient

evidence.note: Typical Ontario practice; on-call providers respond by phone first. Induction share of about 30% is an estimate from general knowledge of Canadian obstetric practice.

steps.name: Assess patient and write labour plan (family physician)
steps.description: The family physician examines the patient, reviews the fetal heart tracing, cervical examination and prenatal risks, and writes admission orders: monitoring method, group B strep antibiotics, pain relief options and whether to induce or augment labour. Overnight the order is often given by phone and the bedside assessment follows.

control.basis: Public Hospitals Act: only a physician or midwife with privileges may order treatment for an inpatient

evidence.note: Typical Ontario practice; on-call providers respond by phone first. Induction share of about 30% is an estimate from general knowledge of Canadian obstetric practice.

steps.name: Assess patient and write labour plan (midwife)
steps.description: The midwife examines the patient, reviews the fetal heart tracing, cervical examination and prenatal risks, and writes admission orders: monitoring method, group B strep antibiotics, pain relief options and whether to induce or augment labour. Overnight the order is often given by phone and the bedside assessment follows.

control.basis: Public Hospitals Act: only a physician or midwife with privileges may order treatment for an inpatient

evidence.note: Typical Ontario practice; on-call providers respond by phone first. Induction share of about 30% is an estimate from general knowledge of Canadian obstetric practice.

steps.name: Start induction of labour
steps.description: The nurse checks the induction order against the unit protocol, runs a baseline fetal heart tracing, inserts or assists with cervical ripening (prostaglandin or balloon) or starts an oxytocin infusion on a pump, and documents each dose change and the tracing at set intervals.

error.defect_description: Oxytocin rate error or excessive contractions not acted on quickly.

control.basis: High-alert medication (oxytocin) protocol with independent double check

evidence.note: Induction steps from general knowledge of Ontario practice; the wait is for a room or a nurse to start a planned induction.

steps.name: Monitor ripening until active labour
steps.description: While cervical ripening works, the nurse checks contractions, the fetal heart and vital signs at set intervals, re-examines or calls the provider, and steps up to oxytocin when the cervix is favourable. The patient keeps the room for many hours, which is the main reason rooms run out.

evidence.note: Elapsed time is the physiological time to active labour after ripening (author's estimate of 2 to 20 hours); the patient is not queued, so the wait cause is none.

steps.name: Give one-to-one care in active labour
steps.description: The nurse stays with the patient through active labour: listens to the fetal heart by intermittent auscultation or reads the continuous monitor, records contractions, vital signs and fluid balance, supports breathing and position changes, and calls the provider when the tracing or progress is abnormal. Much of the time goes to classifying and documenting the tracing.

error.defect_description: Abnormal fetal heart pattern classified late or not escalated.

control.basis: SOGC fetal health surveillance guideline and unit 1:1 labour support policy; Accreditation Canada obstetrics standards

evidence.note: One-to-one support and fetal surveillance duties from kelly2022; duration of active labour after admission (1.5 to 10 hours) is the author's estimate from general obstetric knowledge.

steps.name: Place labour epidural
steps.description: The anesthesiologist reviews the platelet count and consent, places the epidural catheter with the nurse positioning the patient and watching the fetal heart and blood pressure, and writes the infusion order. The patient often waits 10 to 60 minutes while the anesthesiologist finishes a case in the OR; that wait overlaps labour already counted in the previous step.

error.defect_description: Patchy block needing re-site, or hypotension needing treatment.

control.basis: Health Care Consent Act, 1996: informed consent before the procedure

evidence.note: Epidural share of about 55% to 60% of labouring patients and placement time are the author's estimates from general knowledge of Canadian practice.

steps.name: Review labour progress and tracing
steps.description: The provider reviews cervical progress on the partogram and the fetal heart classification with the nurse, decides whether labour can continue, needs oxytocin augmentation, or should end in a caesarean for failure to progress or an abnormal tracing. Family physicians and midwives call the on-call obstetrician for this decision when labour is abnormal.

control.basis: Decision to operate rests with the attending obstetrician (hospital medical staff rules)

evidence.note: Intrapartum caesarean share of 21% of labouring patients makes the total caesarean rate about 31% with 13% booked caesareans, matching the 31.7% Canadian rate in 2021-2022 (cihi_stays); the split between booked and in-labour caesareans is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Coach pushing in the second stage
steps.description: At full dilation the nurse coaches pushing, listens to the fetal heart every five minutes or watches the monitor, prepares the delivery table and baby warmer, and pages the provider when the birth is near. With an epidural the second stage is usually longer.

error.defect_description: Provider paged late; nurse catches the baby.

next.condition: provider at home must come in

evidence.note: Second-stage duration (20 minutes to 3 hours) from general obstetric knowledge.

steps.name: Drive in to attend the birth
steps.description: At night and on weekends the on-call obstetrician, family physician or midwife leaves home when paged and drives to the hospital, usually arriving while the patient is still pushing.

evidence.note: About 30% of births happen when the attending provider is not in the building (nights, weekends); 10 to 40 minute drives in a suburban region. Author's estimate.

steps.name: Conduct the vaginal birth
steps.description: The provider gowns, guides the birth of the head and shoulders, uses vacuum or forceps when the second stage stalls or the tracing worsens, clamps and cuts the cord and hands the baby skin to skin or to the second nurse.

error.defect_description: Perineal tear or shoulder dystocia complicating the birth.

evidence.note: Birth attendance times from general obstetric knowledge; family physicians and midwives attend part of these births (see assumptions).

steps.name: Assess and support the newborn
steps.description: A second nurse dries and stimulates the baby, scores Apgars at one and five minutes, starts ventilation if the baby does not breathe well, and calls the paediatrician by the unit's criteria. The baby is weighed, given vitamin K and eye prophylaxis per orders, and banded with matching identification.

error.defect_description: Mother and baby identification bands mismatched.

control.basis: Newborn identification and infant security policy: matching bands applied before mother and baby are separated

evidence.note: Second nurse at each birth and paediatric call criteria are standard Ontario practice (Neonatal Resuscitation Program); shares are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Deliver placenta and repair tears
steps.description: The provider delivers the placenta with an oxytocin injection, inspects it, examines and sutures any perineal tear, and estimates or weighs blood loss with the nurse. Heavy bleeding starts the postpartum haemorrhage protocol.

evidence.note: Third-stage tasks from general obstetric knowledge; haemorrhage share of about 5% to 7% is an estimate.

steps.name: Stabilize the newborn (paediatrician)
steps.description: The paediatrician comes to the room or OR, takes over resuscitation or assessment, decides whether the baby can stay with the mother or needs the NICU, and writes newborn orders.

next.condition: return to third stage of labour

evidence.note: Paediatrician attendance time from general knowledge of Ontario level II units; on-call response time estimated.

steps.name: Recover mother and baby in the room
steps.description: For about two hours the nurse checks the mother's blood pressure, uterus and bleeding every 15 minutes, supports skin-to-skin contact and the first breastfeed, records the baby's temperature and breathing, and removes the epidural catheter.

evidence.note: Two-hour immediate recovery with 15-minute checks is standard practice; author's knowledge.

steps.name: Manage postpartum haemorrhage
steps.description: The obstetrician leads the haemorrhage protocol with nurses: uterine massage, extra uterotonic drugs, a second IV, blood tests and a crossmatch order to the blood bank, and repair or transfer to the OR when bleeding continues. Severe cases are reported in the incident system.

control.basis: Obstetrical haemorrhage protocol and massive transfusion protocol

evidence.note: Haemorrhage protocol steps from general obstetric knowledge; durations estimated.

steps.name: Give spinal anaesthetic in the obstetrical OR
steps.description: The anesthesiologist checks the patient, places a spinal or tops up the labour epidural (general anaesthetic only in true emergencies), and monitors her through the operation. The case waits when both obstetrical rooms are in use or the anesthesiologist is in the main OR.

control.basis: Surgical safety checklist briefing (Accreditation Canada required organizational practice)

evidence.note: Anaesthesia times and OR waits are the author's estimate; urgent cases are done within about 30 minutes by convention, booked ones wait behind emergencies.

steps.name: Perform the caesarean section
steps.description: The obstetrician performs the caesarean with a surgical assistant (a second obstetrician or a family physician), delivers the baby to the nurse or paediatrician at the warmer, closes the uterus and abdomen and writes the operative note and post-operative orders.

error.defect_description: Surgical count discrepancy or bladder injury.

control.basis: Surgical safety checklist time-out and sign-out

evidence.note: Caesarean duration of 35 to 90 minutes from general surgical knowledge; people = 2 counts the surgeon and the surgical assistant.

steps.name: Decide on caesarean and call the team
steps.description: The obstetrician explains the reason for a caesarean, gets written consent, books the obstetrical OR and pages the anesthesiologist, the paediatrician when indicated and the nurses who will scrub and circulate. The urgency category sets how fast the team must move.

control.basis: Health Care Consent Act, 1996: informed consent to surgery

evidence.note: Consent and team call-out from general knowledge of Ontario birthing units.

steps.name: Scrub, circulate and count in the OR
steps.description: Two labour and delivery nurses run the obstetrical OR: one scrubs and passes instruments, the other circulates, receives the baby when no paediatrician is present, and both count sponges, needles and instruments before closing.

control.basis: Surgical count standard (ORNAC) and surgical safety checklist

evidence.note: In Ontario community birthing units the labour nurses usually staff the obstetrical OR; author's knowledge.

steps.name: Recover mother after caesarean
steps.description: The nurse monitors the mother in the recovery area or her room: vital signs, sensation returning after the spinal, wound, bleeding and pain, while supporting skin-to-skin contact and the first feed.

evidence.note: Post-anaesthetic recovery in the birthing unit, 1 to 2.5 hours; author's estimate.

steps.name: Prepare patient for booked caesarean
steps.description: The patient arrives fasting at the booked time; the nurse checks consent, bloodwork and the pre-operative checklist, starts an IV and gives prophylactic antibiotics and antacid. Booked cases are often bumped by emergency caesareans in labour.

error.defect_description: Missing bloodwork or consent delays the start.

evidence.note: Booked caesareans arrive about two hours early and are displaced by urgent cases; author's estimate.

steps.name: Document the birth and enter the BORN record
steps.description: The nurse completes the birth record in the hospital information system (times, method, blood loss, Apgars, medications) and enters the mother and baby birth data in the BORN Information System, often after the recovery period or at the end of the shift.

error.defect_description: Missing or inconsistent BORN fields (for example labour type or analgesia).

control.basis: Provincial perinatal data collection through BORN Ontario (prescribed registry under PHIPA)

evidence.note: Double entry into the hospital chart and BORN was common in 2019-2022 where the systems were not integrated; times estimated.

steps.name: Register the newborn
steps.description: The unit clerk creates the newborn's encounter in the hospital information system linked to the mother's, prints identification band labels for the nurse to check against the bands applied at birth, and updates the unit board.

error.defect_description: Newborn registered under the wrong mother or with a wrong sex or birth time.

evidence.note: Newborn registration practice from general knowledge; NICU admission share of about 8% is the author's estimate for a level II unit.

steps.name: Transfer the baby to the NICU
steps.description: The nurse takes the baby to the NICU in a transport incubator with the paediatrician's orders, gives report to the NICU nurse, and then phones report on the mother to the mother-baby unit and moves her there.

evidence.note: Transfer practice from general knowledge; the wait is for a NICU bassinet or postpartum bed.

steps.name: Hand over mother and baby to the postpartum nurse
steps.description: When a mother-baby bed is ready the nurse gives a bedside or phone report to the postpartum nurse (birth details, blood loss, feeding, newborn findings) and moves mother and baby together. The room is then released for cleaning.

error.defect_description: Hand-over omits a risk such as GBS status or a low blood sugar plan.

evidence.note: Hand-over and the wait for a postpartum bed (up to several hours when the mother-baby unit is full) are the author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Caesarean in labour
exceptions.description: Labour stalls or the fetal heart tracing is abnormal; the obstetrician decides on a caesarean and the obstetrical OR team is called.

exceptions.name: Booked caesarean bumped
exceptions.description: A booked caesarean waits for hours because emergency caesareans take the obstetrical rooms.

exceptions.name: Postpartum haemorrhage
exceptions.description: Heavy bleeding after birth starts the haemorrhage protocol and a blood bank order.

exceptions.name: Newborn needs NICU
exceptions.description: The paediatrician admits the baby to the NICU and the mother goes to the postpartum unit alone.

exceptions.name: Long induction
exceptions.description: Cervical ripening takes most of a day, holding a labour room.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from admission to the birthing unit to hand-over to postpartum or NICU

evidence.note: Author's estimate: about 4 to 8 hours of active labour after admission, up to an hour of pushing, 2 hours of recovery and up to an hour waiting for a postpartum bed for most patients, and most of a day for inductions (about 30%). Consistent with an average total birth stay of 2.1 days (cihi_stays) of which about 1.5 days is postpartum. No published Ontario figure for this interval was found.

benchmarks.unit: days, whole hospital stay for giving birth

evidence.note: Caesarean section stays averaged 2.7 days.

pain_points.description: Labour rooms are held for many hours by inductions and recovering patients, so new labouring patients wait in triage when the unit is full.

evidence.note: Author's knowledge of Ontario birthing unit flow; no measured wait data found.

pain_points.description: Nurses spend much of active labour classifying and charting the fetal heart tracing at the station, and re-enter birth data in BORN.

evidence.note: Observed in a Canadian unit by kelly2022; double entry into BORN is the author's knowledge.

pain_points.description: Booked caesareans are bumped by emergencies because the unit has only two obstetrical rooms and one anaesthesia team.

evidence.note: Author's knowledge of Ontario community hospital obstetrical OR scheduling.

pain_points.description: The hand-over waits for a postpartum bed when the mother-baby unit is full, which keeps the labour room blocked.

evidence.note: Author's knowledge; mother-baby occupancy is high on weekday mornings before discharges.

sources.title: Halton Healthcare 2021-2022 Annual Community Report (By the Numbers)
sources.supports: 2021/22: 4,690 babies born; 161,049 emergency department visits; 37,964 dialysis visits; 62,508 mental health and addictions ambulatory visits; 5,228 staff.

sources.title: Halton Healthcare 2020-2021 Annual Community Report (By the Numbers)
sources.supports: 2020/21: 4,277 babies born; 126,357 emergency department visits; 37,171 dialysis visits; 89,823 addictions and mental health visits; top five in Ontario for patients on home dialysis (Ontario Renal Network, March 2021).

sources.title: Hospital stays in Canada, 2021-2022
sources.supports: Giving birth was the most common reason for hospitalization, average acute stay 2.1 days; caesarean section the most common inpatient surgery, average stay 2.7 days; total caesarean rate 31.7% in 2021-2022, up from 28.8% in 2017-2018.

sources.title: Using Institutional Ethnography to Explicate the Everyday Realities of Nurses' Work in Labor and Delivery (P. Kelly, M. Quance, N. Snow, C. Porr), Global Qualitative Nursing Research
sources.supports: In a Canadian labour and delivery unit, the SOGC fetal health surveillance guideline, CAPWHN perinatal nursing standards and the unit's 1:1 labour support policy say women in active labour should receive continuous labour support; SOGC recommends intermittent auscultation for low-risk labour and continuous electronic fetal monitoring for high-risk labour; nurses spent much of the shift interpreting and documenting the fetal monitor tracing and described heavy defensive documentation.

assumptions: Describes the common practice of an Ontario community hospital birthing unit in 2019-2022, not Halton Healthcare's own procedures.

The organisation file lists dx-blood-transfusion as a trigger of this process; a blood product does not start a birth, so it is recorded as a standing input and the blood order as an output. Booked caesareans arrive from the surgical schedule (sx-or-scheduling, or_schedule, 13% of cases), a trigger the organisation file lacks.

Steps s09, s11, s12, s14, s17, s19 and s20 use the obstetrician role. In practice family physicians and midwives conduct their own patients' vaginal births (about 40% of vaginal births) and call the obstetrician for abnormal labour; costs in these steps are therefore somewhat overstated.

Caesarean rate: 13% booked plus 21% of labouring patients gives about 31%, matching the 31.7% Canadian rate in 2021-2022. Induction (30%), epidural (55%), postpartum haemorrhage (6%), paediatrician attendance (10%) and NICU admission (8%) are tier C estimates.
The anesthesiologist wait for an epidural and the provider's drive in overlap labour time and are recorded with no extra wait (concurrent_with), so the simulated cycle counts only elapsed time.
Only one resource figure is used for the whole corporation: the 16 labour rooms and 2 obstetrical ORs in the organisation file, spread across sites.

Labour nurse FTE (50) is set by around-the-clock room staffing rather than hands-on minutes; the simulated hands-on time implies fewer FTE because one-to-one nurses also cover triage, idle rooms and breaks. Loaded costs come from the organisation file (wage times 1.35; physician figures are gross OHIP earnings).
